title: The Way of a Pilgrim
hook: an anonymous Russian wanderer tries to pray without ceasing, using the Jesus Prayer

segments.voice: Yesterday: Seraphim in the snow, and Motovilov, who felt peace and warmth in a winter forest. Your line was acquire the spirit of peace.

Pray without ceasing. The line is read out in church, and a man standing there feels it catch like a hook in cloth. Without ceasing? How? People have to work, and eat, and sleep. So he leaves, with a knapsack, some dried bread and a Bible, and starts walking, asking preachers and monks how it's done. Nobody gives him an answer that works. A little book tells all this, in his own voice. He never gives his name. He calls himself only a wanderer, a pilgrim. Today: The Way of a Pilgrim.

The line is from Paul's first letter to the Thessalonians, in the King James Bible: "Pray without ceasing." The pilgrim wanders until, the book says, he meets an elder, a starets, who finally answers him. The answer is a very short prayer, said over and over: the Jesus Prayer. Its usual words are Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Its roots are in the Gospels. A blind man by the road at Jericho calls out: "Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me." And a tax collector in one of Jesus's parables stands far off and prays: "God be merciful to me a sinner." The elder sets the pilgrim a task: say the prayer a set number of times each day, using a prayer rope to keep his place, and then more. At first it's work, like learning to walk again. Then, the pilgrim says, something shifts. The prayer starts to say itself. It moves from his lips into his heart, falls into the rhythm of his breath, keeps time with his heartbeat. He walks for miles with it running quietly underneath everything, and the world starts to look different: people kinder, trees and grass full of God. That's the book's answer. Not a voice that never stops talking, but a prayer that keeps going underneath, like a heartbeat. It closes a week of faith lived, not only spoken: Crowther, Truth, Tubman, Douglass, the hush harbors, Seraphim, and now a wanderer, walking.

Stand if you can and walk slowly, around the room or down a hall, letting your steps find an easy rhythm. If you pray, use the Jesus Prayer, or just the blind man's words, have mercy on me, one phrase on each step or breath; if you don't, choose one short true line and let it keep time with your feet. When your mind wanders, come back gently.
Jesus Prayer. The short prayer, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner, that the nameless pilgrim learned to say without ceasing.
Your line: pray without ceasing. A short prayer can run quietly under an ordinary day. Day nine hundred twenty-four, done.

howItsDone: Orthodox Christians, and some Catholics and Protestants, pray the Jesus Prayer, often with a prayer rope, repeating it quietly through the day.
